subproblem.title: Borel measurability of the straightened slice-Jacobian integrand F̃
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, B ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} open, χ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} of class C¹ on B, S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} Borel and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) and 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m}, where D = fderiv ℝ and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then F̃ := 1_{S′}·(y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)) : ℝ^{m+1} → [0, ∞] is Borel measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl P) (B : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (χ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl (m + 1)) (S : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ B → MeasurableSet S → Measurable g → Measurable ((B ∩ χ ⁻¹' S).indicator (fun y => g (Φ (χ y)) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (fderiv ℝ χ y (EuclideanSpace.single i.succ 1))) (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (fderiv ℝ χ y (EuclideanSpace.single j.succ 1)))).det)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; D := fderiv ℝ. Let S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S), 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m} and F̃ := S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)). Measurable means Borel measurable.

This is step 8 of the parent proof (slicing_im_creg_box_coarea), where F̃ is the integrand handed to Tonelli. No sibling lemma is used. Mathlib results used: ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, measurable_fderiv_apply_const, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply, continuous_inner, Continuous.matrix_det, Measurable.of_eval and Measurable.indicator. Lean note: the frozen import closure has neither Measurable.inner nor a MeasurableSpace instance on Matrix. So inner products are handled through the continuous map (u, u′) ↦ ⟨u, u′⟩ composed with a measurable pair, and the determinant through the entry function in Fin m → Fin m → ℝ.

1. (Measurable extension of χ.) χ is C¹ on B, hence continuous on B (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Let χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0, which is χ on B and 0 off B. It is Borel measurable by ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, since χ is continuous on the measurable set B and the constant 0 is continuous on Bᶜ.
2. (S′ is Borel.) Since χ̃ = χ on B, S′ = B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S). This set is Borel because B is open and χ̃ is measurable.
3. (Replace χ by χ̃ in the integrand.) For k < m+1 let a_k(y) := DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_k), and for i, j < m let M(y)_{ij} := ⟨a_{i+1}(y), a_{j+1}(y)⟩. Put F̂(y) := g(Φ(χ̃ y))·ofReal √det M(y). Only the outer occurrences of χ become χ̃; Dχ(y) is kept. For y ∈ S′ ⊆ B, χ̃(y) = χ(y), so the integrands of F̃ and of S′.indicator F̂ agree on S′. Set.indicator_congr gives F̃ = S′.indicator F̂. By Measurable.indicator and step 2, it suffices to show that F̂ is measurable.
4. (The factor g∘Φ∘χ̃.) Φ is C¹, hence continuous and measurable. χ̃ is measurable (step 1) and g is measurable, so y ↦ g(Φ(χ̃ y)) is measurable.
5. (The vectors a_k.) Fix k. Then y ↦ Dχ(y)e_k is measurable by measurable_fderiv_apply_const, which holds for any map χ between finite-dimensional spaces. Because Φ is C¹, the map (x, u) ↦ DΦ(x)u on ℝ^{m+1} × ℝ^{m+1} is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply with 1 ≠ 0), hence Borel measurable; the product of these second-countable spaces carries the product Borel σ-algebra. Composing it with the measurable map y ↦ (χ̃ y, Dχ(y)e_k) shows that a_k is measurable.
6. (The entries.) The inner product (u, u′) ↦ ⟨u, u′⟩ on ℝ^P × ℝ^P is continuous (continuous_inner), hence measurable. Composing it with y ↦ (a_{i+1}(y), a_{j+1}(y)) shows that y ↦ M(y)_{ij} is measurable for all i, j < m.
7. (Determinant, square root, ofReal.) The map y ↦ (M(y)_{ij})_{i,j} into Fin m → Fin m → ℝ is measurable (Measurable.of_eval, applied twice). The function N ↦ det(Matrix.of N) on Fin m → Fin m → ℝ is continuous, because det is a polynomial in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det applied to the continuous identity); hence it is measurable. So y ↦ det M(y) is measurable. Real.sqrt is continuous and ENNReal.ofReal is measurable, so y ↦ ofReal √det M(y) is measurable. For m = 0 the matrix is empty with determinant 1, and the same argument applies.
8. (Conclusion.) F̂ is the product of the measurable [0,∞]-valued functions of steps 4 and 7, hence measurable (Measurable.mul). By step 3, F̃ = S′.indicator F̂ is measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0 is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise), so S′ = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S) is Borel.
On S′ replace the outer χ by χ̃ (Set.indicator_congr) and reduce to measurability of F̂ (Measurable.indicator).
a_k(y) := DΦ(χ̃ y)(Dχ(y)e_k) is measurable: measurable_fderiv_apply_const plus the continuous (x,u) ↦ DΦ(x)u (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply).
Inner products via continuous_inner; entries via Measurable.of_eval; det via Continuous.matrix_det on Fin m → Fin m → ℝ; then √, ofReal, and the product with g∘Φ∘χ̃.

audit.reason: The prose and exact one-line type agree. The proof correctly extends χ measurably, replaces only its outer occurrences on the indicator support, and retains Dχ. Derivative evaluation measurability, C¹ joint derivative continuity, continuous inner products and the determinant on the finite entry-function space establish the remaining factors. All eight steps prove global Borel measurability without assuming χ measurable outside B or using another child.

subproblem.title: Area formula through Φ composed with an injective C¹ change of variables χ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P K-Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some K ≥ 0 and c > 0 (c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for w, w′ ∈ Ω). Let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and χ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ of class C¹ on B and injective on B, with χ(B) ⊆ Ω. Let S ⊆ χ(B) be Borel and ψ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}, where D = fderiv ℝ and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then ∫_{Φ(S)} ψ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{S′}(y)·ofReal|det Dχ(y)|·ψ(Φ(χ y))·ofReal(JΦ(χ y)) dLⁿ(y), with Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P and Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (B : Set (Eucl n)) (χ : Eucl n → Eucl n) (S : Set (Eucl n)) (ψ : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ B → InjOn χ B → χ '' B ⊆ Ω → MeasurableSet S → S ⊆ χ '' B → Measurable ψ → ∫⁻ x in Φ '' S, ψ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫⁻ y, (B ∩ χ ⁻¹' S).indicator (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal |(fderiv ℝ χ y).det| * (ψ (Φ (χ y)) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ (χ y) (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det))) y ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
proof_key_steps: Φ is injective and continuous on Ω; Φ(S) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Φ(S)) = S.
area_formula for Φ on Ω with A := Φ(S): ∫_{Φ(S)} ψ dHⁿ = ∫_S ψ∘Φ·ofReal JΦ dLⁿ.
S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S) is Borel (piecewise extension χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0), χ(S′) = S, HasFDerivWithinAt χ (Dχ y) S′ y, and χ is injective on S′.
lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul along χ on S′ with G₀ := ψ∘Φ·ofReal JΦ, then lintegral_indicator.

audit.reason: All hypotheses, measures, determinant factors and indicator support match the exact Lean type. The proof establishes the Borel images/preimages and their identities, applies area_formula, and then verifies injectivity and within-set derivatives for change of variables along χ. The pinned change-of-variables theorem requires no measurability assumption on its integrand. All eight steps are complete, and the sole child dependency is correctly directed to area_formula.

subproblem.title: Area formula on the slices {y₀ = t} of a straightened chart (B, χ)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝ^{m+1}, and Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, K-Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Let B ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open and χ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} of class C¹ on B and Λ-Lipschitz on B, with χ(B) ⊆ Ω. Assume |v − v′| ≤ |χ([t,v]) − χ([t,v′])| whenever t ∈ ℝ, v, v′ ∈ ℝ^m and [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B, where [t,v] := (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)). Let S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] be Borel. Put S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S), 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m} and F̃ := 1_{S′}·(y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)). Then for every t ∈ ℝ, with σ_t(v) := Φ(χ([t,v])) and S′_t := {v ∈ ℝ^m : [t,v] ∈ S′}, ∫_{σ_t(S′_t)} g dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃([t,v]) dL^m(v), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and L^m := volume on ℝ^m.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; L^k = volume on ℝ^k; H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; D := fderiv ℝ.
- For t ∈ ℝ and v ∈ ℝ^m, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) is the point (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}). In Lean, EuclideanSpace.equiv is ofLp and its inverse is toLp 2, so [t,v]_0 = t and [t,v]_{i+1} = v_i hold by simp (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ).
- S′ := B ∩ χ⁻¹(S).
- 𝒥(y) := √det(⟨DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{i+1}), DΦ(χ y)(Dχ(y)e_{j+1})⟩)_{i,j<m}.
- F̃ := S′.indicator (y ↦ g(Φ(χ y))·ofReal 𝒥(y)).
Fix K, c > 0 and Λ from the hypotheses, and fix t ∈ ℝ. Write e(v) := [t,v], σ(v) := Φ(χ(e v)), B_t := e⁻¹(B) and S′_t := e⁻¹(S′) = {v : [t,v] ∈ B ∩ χ⁻¹(S)}. The claim is ∫_{σ(S′_t)} g dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃(e v) dL^m(v).

This is steps 1, 3 (slice part) and 10 of the parent proof (slicing_im_creg_box_coarea). The slice-set identity of the parent's step 11 stays in the parent, so neither f nor h appears here. Sibling lemma used: area_formula (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables), with n := m. Mathlib results used: Lusin–Souslin MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn, ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, LipschitzOnWith.comp and the chain rule HasFDerivAt.comp.

1. (The linear part ι.) Define ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} by ι(z) := [0,z]. Using Fin.cases on the index, ι(z) has component 0 equal to 0 and component j+1 equal to z_j. So ι is linear, checked componentwise, and since ℝ^m is finite-dimensional it is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Again componentwise, e(v) = e(0) + ι(v) for every v. Hence e is continuous, and HasFDerivAt e ι v holds for every v (a constant plus a continuous linear map).
2. (Properties of ι.)
(a) ι(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < m. Compare components. At 0 both are 0. At j+1 the left side is (e_i)_j = [j = i] and the right side is [j+1 = i+1] = [j = i] (Fin.succ_inj).
(b) |ι z| = |z|. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ, |ι z|² = 0² + Σ_j z_j² = |z|².
Hence |e(v) − e(v′)| = |ι(v − v′)| = |v − v′|, and e is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
3. (Slice sets.) B_t = e⁻¹(B) is open, since B is open and e is continuous. S′ is Borel: χ is continuous on B (C¹ on B), χ̃ := B.piecewise χ 0 is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise), and S′ = B ∩ χ̃⁻¹(S) because χ̃ = χ on B. So S′_t = e⁻¹(S′) is Borel, as e is continuous and hence measurable. Also S′_t ⊆ B_t.
4. (σ is Lipschitz on B_t.) σ = Φ ∘ χ ∘ e, where:
- e is 1-Lipschitz and maps B_t into B;
- χ is Λ-Lipschitz on B and maps B into Ω (χ(B) ⊆ Ω);
- Φ is K-Lipschitz on Ω.
Applying LipschitzOnWith.comp twice, σ is K·(Λ·1)-Lipschitz on B_t, and in particular continuous on B_t.
5. (σ is antilipschitz and injective on B_t.) Let v, v′ ∈ B_t, so [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B. The slice hypothesis gives |v − v′| ≤ |χ(e v) − χ(e v′)|. Since χ(e v), χ(e v′) ∈ χ(B) ⊆ Ω, the antilipschitz bound of Φ then gives c|v − v′| ≤ c|χ(e v) − χ(e v′)| ≤ |σ(v) − σ(v′)|. Hence σ is injective on B_t: if σ(v) = σ(v′), then c|v − v′| ≤ 0 with c > 0, so v = v′.
6. (A_t := σ(S′_t) is Borel, and B_t ∩ σ⁻¹(A_t) = S′_t.) σ is continuous (step 4) and injective (step 5) on the Borel set S′_t ⊆ B_t, and ℝ^m is Polish, so A_t is Borel by Lusin–Souslin. For the set identity, S′_t ⊆ B_t ∩ σ⁻¹(A_t) is clear. Conversely, if v ∈ B_t and σ(v) = σ(v′) with v′ ∈ S′_t ⊆ B_t, then v = v′ ∈ S′_t by step 5.
7. (Area formula for σ.) Apply area_formula with P, n := m, the map σ, the open set B_t (step 3), A := A_t and weight g. Its hypotheses hold:
- σ is Lipschitz on B_t (step 4) and c-antilipschitz on B_t (step 5);
- A_t ⊆ σ(B_t), because S′_t ⊆ B_t;
- A_t is Borel (step 6), hence H^m-null-measurable;
- g is Borel, hence a.e.-measurable.
Its third conclusion together with step 6 gives ∫_{A_t} g dH^m = ∫_{S′_t} g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v)) dL^m(v), where Jσ(v) := √det(⟨Dσ(v)e_i, Dσ(v)e_j⟩)_{i,j<m}. The cases m = 0 and B_t = ∅ are covered uniformly, so no case split is needed.
8. (Derivative of σ.) Φ is C¹, hence differentiable, so HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ(x)) x for all x. For y ∈ B, χ is differentiable at y because B is open and χ is C¹ on B, so HasFDerivAt χ (Dχ(y)) y. For v ∈ B_t, the chain rule and step 1 give HasFDerivAt σ (DΦ(χ(e v)) ∘L Dχ(e v) ∘L ι) v. Hence Dσ(v) = DΦ(χ(e v)) ∘ Dχ(e v) ∘ ι (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). By step 2(a), Dσ(v)e_i = DΦ(χ(e v))(Dχ(e v)e_{i+1}) for i < m. Therefore Jσ(v) = 𝒥(e v) for v ∈ B_t.
9. (Conclusion.) Compare the integrands pointwise:
- if v ∈ S′_t, then e(v) ∈ S′, and by step 8, F̃(e v) = g(Φ(χ(e v)))·ofReal 𝒥(e v) = g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v));
- if v ∉ S′_t, then e(v) ∉ S′ and F̃(e v) = 0.
So v ↦ F̃(e v) equals S′_t.indicator (v ↦ g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v))). Since S′_t is Borel, lintegral_indicator and lintegral_congr give ∫_{ℝ^m} F̃(e v) dL^m(v) = ∫_{S′_t} g(σ v)·ofReal(Jσ(v)) dL^m(v). By step 7 this equals ∫_{A_t} g dH^m, and A_t = σ(S′_t) is exactly the image set in the statement. ∎

B_t := e⁻¹(B) is open; S′_t := e⁻¹(B ∩ χ⁻¹(S)) is Borel (piecewise extension of χ) and S′_t ⊆ B_t.
σ_t = Φ∘χ∘e is Lipschitz (LipschitzOnWith.comp) and c-antilipschitz (slice hypothesis plus antilipschitz Φ) on B_t; A_t := σ_t(S′_t) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and B_t ∩ σ_t⁻¹(A_t) = S′_t.
